counterfactual_missing_items: R1 lacks explicit mention of dissemination across multiple sites (lung, spine, toe).
R4 lacks any support for a primary diagnosis of chronic kidney disease; urine findings are secondary to infection.
decisive_items: Biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus.
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression.
induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert and subsequently grew MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid.
response.rationale: C1 directly captures the disseminated nature of tuberculosis with raw spans from three distinct anatomical sites (lung, spine, toe) and microbiologic confirmation. R1 is a correct but less specific label, missing the dissemination qualifier. R4 is a red herring; urine abnormalities are explained by the underlying infection and do not constitute a primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Urine findings are nonspecific and secondary to the disseminated infection; no raw support for chronic kidney disease as the primary diagnosis.
